objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have practiced and developed the sub-skills of listening for specific information and detail in the context of how AI is expected to affect the job market.
materials:
- BTN Newsbreak 4 June 2026 - AI Report (YouTube video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0gOqzcztjzA)
- Bespoke listening worksheet with gapped outline and comprehension questions
- Transcript and answer key

stages.stage_aim: To get students thinking about AI in the workplace and what it might mean for different jobs
stages.procedure:
- Elicit what students know about AI. Ask: "Have you used ChatGPT or other AI tools? What for?" Let a few students share experiences.
- Display the question: "Will AI take our jobs?" Put students in pairs to brainstorm jobs that AI could do instead of humans (1 min). Collect ideas on the board.
- Narrow the focus: ask whether students think AI is mostly helpful or mostly a risk for workers. Show a quick hands-up poll.
- Introduce the listening: "We're going to watch a BTN Newsbreak report about AI and jobs. The reporter shares what a big company called Deloitte found. We'll watch it three times, each time with a different focus."
- Interaction: T-Ss, Ss-Ss

stages.stage: Pre-listening — Outline Strategy and Key Vocabulary
stages.stage_aim: To introduce the outline note-taking format and pre-teach essential vocabulary for the listening task
stages.procedure:
- Distribute the worksheet. Project the outline format on the board. Explain that an outline uses Roman numerals (I, II, III) for main ideas and capital letters (A, B) for sub-points.
- Tell students they will watch the AI segment three times. Each time they focus on one part of the outline and fill the gaps with words from the video (max 3 words per gap).
- Pre-teach key vocabulary from the transcript: disrupted, enhanced, occupations, empathy, thoughtfully. Use simple definitions and a context sentence for each. Check understanding with quick concept questions.
- Set the listening frame: "Part 1 is about which jobs are at risk. The key information comes from a company called Deloitte. Listen for numbers and job names."
- Interaction: T-Ss

stages.stage_aim: To listen for specific information about which jobs are most likely to be affected by AI and complete the first section of the outline
stages.procedure:
- Play the first part of the AI segment (0:00–0:43 on the YouTube video). Students complete gaps I.A.1–I.B.1 on the outline.
- Pause the video. Students answer Comprehension Questions 1–3 for Part 1.
- Elicit answers from 2–3 students. Check outline gaps as a class. Clarify any confusion about "disrupted" and "82 occupations."
- Set the listening frame for Part 2: "Now the report shifts — not all AI effects are negative. Listen for which industries AI can actually help."
- Interaction: S, T-Ss

stages.stage: Listening Part 2 — Jobs Enhanced by AI
stages.stage_aim: To listen for detail about how AI can benefit certain jobs that rely on human skills
stages.procedure:
- Play the second part of the AI segment (0:44–1:02). Students complete gaps II.A.1–II.B.2 on the outline.
- Pause the video. Students answer Comprehension Questions 1–3 for Part 2.
- Brief class feedback. Focus on the three human skills (creativity, judgement, empathy) — check students can explain each one in simple terms.
- Set the listening frame for Part 3: "The final part talks about what the government is doing with AI and what experts say young people should do. Listen for the name of the AI system."
- Interaction: S, T-Ss

stages.stage_aim: To listen for specific information about the AI system Mythos and expert advice for young people
stages.procedure:
- Play the final part of the AI segment (1:02–1:27). Students complete gaps III.A.1–III.B.2 on the outline.
- Pause the video. Students answer Comprehension Questions 1–3 for Part 3.
- Class feedback. Highlight the expert advice: learn to work with AI and use it thoughtfully. Ask students what "thoughtfully" means in their own words.
- Collect worksheets if desired.
- Interaction: S, T-Ss

stages.stage_aim: To introduce simple phrases for expressing opinions and responding to others in a structured discussion
stages.procedure:
- Refer students to Part 4 of the worksheet. Display the discussion phrases on the board: introducing a point ("I think that ... because ...", "In my opinion, ...", "It seems to me that ...", "One thing I noticed was ...") and responding to others ("That's a good point. I'd add that ...", "I see what you mean. However, ...", "I hadn't thought of it that way.", "That's interesting. But what about ...?").
- Model a short exchange with a volunteer. Show how to state an opinion, give a reason, and respond to a partner's view.
- Emphasise that both partners should speak and that acknowledging the other person's idea makes the discussion stronger.
- Interaction: T-Ss

stages.stage_aim: To apply ideas from the listening to personal opinions, using the discussion phrases practiced
stages.procedure:
- Refer students to the two Think-Pair-Share questions on the worksheet.
- Question 1 (scaffolded): "Which jobs do you think are most at risk from AI? Use at least one piece of evidence from the video." Point out the suggested structure: say what you think → give evidence from the video → summarise.
- Question 2 (free practice, no scaffolding): "How can young people prepare for a future with AI? What skills should they learn?" No structure provided — students formulate their own response.
- Think: Students write brief notes individually (2 min). Pair: Students discuss both questions in pairs, using the discussion techniques (3 min). Share: Elicit responses from 2–3 pairs for each question. Provide content and language feedback (2 min).
- Interaction: S, Ss-Ss, T-Ss
